assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from proglucagon-derived incretin biology to receptor agonists that treat type 2 diabetes and obesity, is a rare case of basic hormone physiology becoming a transformative therapy with large population-level impact. The discovery chain is clear and the clinical effect is extensive, including cardiovascular and renal benefit signals.
assessment.attribution: Drucker, Holst and Mojsov cover the physiology, the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide characterization and incretin-effect work. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen is the pharmaceutical development figure and is left out to keep the prize on discovery, but this is a genuine allocation judgment.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs and large outcome trials. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for identifying the active peptide form is contested and I cannot verify the precise priority claims.
Whether drug development (Knudsen) should be recognized alongside physiology is unresolved.
Other contributors such as Habener are not in the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defines how cytosolic DNA is sensed and converted into interferon and inflammatory responses, with a new second messenger (cGAMP). It reshaped understanding of innate immunity, autoimmunity, infection and tumour immunity, a conceptual advance of broad importance.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger; Barber identified STING. Ishikawa shares the STING discovery and Sun/Wu were in Chen's group, but a two-person prize is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed and widely adopted. Therapeutic translation (STING agonists and antagonists) has not yet delivered an approved drug, so the clinical impact is still emerging, though the basic science is mature.
uncertainties: Whether Ishikawa should be included alongside Barber for the STING identification is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with millisecond precision and transformed circuit research across model systems. Originality and methodological impact are exceptionally high, though it is a tool rather than a disease mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann characterized channelrhodopsin; Deisseroth built the neuronal tool kit and applied it. Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenboeck all have strong claims, so any three-person split leaves legitimate omissions.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a tool with thousands of independent applications; first clinical use in vision restoration is emerging. Timely.
uncertainties: Credit conflict among Boyden, Deisseroth, Miesenboeck and the microbial opsin discoverers is substantial.
Whether a methods advance fits the prize's physiology or medicine remit is for the committee to weigh.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed an organelle-to-nucleus signaling pathway (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing) governing proteostasis, with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. A clear, original and conceptually clean discovery.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently delineated the pathway in yeast and mammalian cells and are the natural pair. The inclusion of other pioneers such as Ron or Kaufman is not available in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed and deeply embedded in textbooks. Direct therapeutic translation is limited so far.
uncertainties: Clinical impact is modest compared with other candidates.
Contributions of others in the PERK/ATF6 arms are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR is a central regulator of growth and nutrient sensing, from yeast genetics to mTORC1/2 biology with implications for cancer, metabolism, ageing and immunosuppression. Originality and breadth are very high.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically and its role in growth control; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and key pathway components. Schreiber's rapamycin chemistry matters but is less central. Sabatini's inclusion is complicated by a documented professional controversy I cannot assess.
assessment.maturity: Mature with extensive independent confirmation; rapalogs are clinically used. Timely.
uncertainties: Sabatini's contested professional history may bear on suitability.
Roles of Brown, Sabers, Sabatini and Schreiber in mTOR discovery are not separable from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living therapy. The clinical impact is high and the concept (receptor engineering of T cells) is original.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led early costimulatory CAR design and clinical translation; Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy work is foundational but a different component. Eshhar and others are not in the credit list.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and multi-year follow-up; limitations remain in solid tumours and toxicity. Recognition is reasonably timely.
uncertainties: Compound discovery with credit divided between design, preclinical and clinical work.
Rosenberg and Eshhar claims are not resolved by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Lgr5-based adult stem-cell organoids created self-organizing, expandable three-dimensional human tissue cultures that transformed disease modeling, drug testing and stem-cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell and organoid work; Sato was first author of the key 2009 and 2011 organoid papers. This pair is supported by the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated and widely adopted, though clinical translation is still early. Plausibly timely but the field is still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with other organoid pioneers is not reflected in the credit list.
Clinical impact has not yet matured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 as a regulator of cell survival defined a class of apoptosis control genes distinct from proliferation drivers and underpins venetoclax therapy, linking a basic discovery to cancer treatment.
assessment.attribution: Adams and Cory characterized Bcl-2 dysregulation and the family; Vaux showed its anti-apoptotic function. Strasser would also be plausible but three names are the cap, and Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer are absent.
assessment.maturity: Mature with a validated drug and consistent confirmation. The apoptosis field has been recognized previously (2002), which complicates timing.
uncertainties: Precedent of the 2002 prize on programmed cell death.
Credit for BCL-2 discovery involves people not in the list.
